t: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for any activity or the publication or distribution of literature that in any way tends to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal on which Congressional action is not complete other than to communicate to Members of Congress as described in 18 U.S.C. 1913.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to "public support or opposition" and communicating with Members of Congress signal public involvement. But this is a funding restriction that bars the use of appropriations for publicity or propaganda on pending legislation. It sets up no process for outside parties to be consulted, comment, sit on a committee, or sue over a federal decision, and the only communication it mentions is with Members of Congress, who are inside the federal government.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for any activity or the publication or distribution of literature that in any way tends to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal

opus.w: This is a limit on spending: it stops agencies from using appropriated money to stir up public support for or opposition to pending legislation. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. The only communication it allows is with Members of Congress, and Congress is inside the federal government, so the mention of the public and of communication does not count as participation.
opus.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for any activity or the publication or distribution of literature that in any way tends to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "public support or opposition" and "communicate to Members of Congress" describe people taking part in government. That reading fails. This provision only limits how appropriated funds may be spent, barring agency lobbying campaigns aimed at the public. The one communication it allows goes to Members of Congress, who are inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted on any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section restricts the use of funds for public advocacy and limits permissible communication to Members of Congress. Since Congress is part of the federal government, communication with it is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with outside parties. The text does not require consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act shall be available for any activity or the publication or distribution of literature that in any way tends to promote public support or opposition to any legislative proposal on which Congressional action is not complete other than to communicate to Members of Congress as described in 18 U.S.C. 1913.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that restricting communication to "Members of Congress" implies a form of participation or consultation with the legislative branch. However, Congress is explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, any interaction solely between federal agencies and Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. The section actually restricts communication with the general public, rather than requiring it.
